newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian, Hungarian banks sign credit conventions.
newsitem.headline: Romanian, Hungarian banks sign credit conventions.

text.p: Romania's leading state-owned bank Banca Romana de Comert Exterior SA - Bancorex said on Tuesday it had signed two credit conventions with a Hungarian bank to support Hungary's commodities exports to Romania.
The short- and respectively medium-term conventions had been signed with the Hungarian Export Import Bank, a Bancorex statement said.
It said the short-term credit was a one-year revolving credit worth $2 million. The interest rate was three-month LIBOR plus 1.625 percent annually.
The medium-term credit is a five-year loan worth $10 million to be paid back in "equal and consecutive instalments every six months".
The credit carries interest equivalent with six-month LIBOR plus 1.25 percent per annum for periods of up to four years and six-month LIBOR plus 1.5 percent annually for periods of over four years.
The Hungarian Export Import Bank will finance 85 percent of the worth of export-import contracts, with the importer covering 15 percent, the statement said.
It said the conventions had been signed during the Hungarian president's visit to Romania.
Hungary's Arpad Goncz arrived in Bucharest on Sunday for a three-day visit, the first by a Hungarian head of state for 70 years, to boost relations at all levels.
